title: FIRST PSIRT capability and cumulative maturity profile
claim_boundary: This public profile is a paraphrased organization assessment template. Repository controls may supply supporting evidence but cannot establish that a PSIRT service operates, has sufficient capacity, or has reached a FIRST maturity level.

rows.capability: Executive sponsorship, scope, budget, roles, and initial response policies are documented and current.
rows.threat_or_failure: An ad-hoc team lacks authority, resources, or policy to require consistent product vulnerability response.
rows.limitations: A document alone does not establish operating authority, staffing capacity, or consistent execution.

rows.capability: Internal teams, customers, finders, coordinators, suppliers, and downstream users have named communication routes.
rows.threat_or_failure: A valid report or urgent remediation decision stalls because ownership and communication routes are unknown.
rows.limitations: A contact list does not prove reachability, trust, or response timeliness.

rows.capability: Public and internal vulnerability intake accepts protected reports, acknowledges receipt, and preserves reporter confidentiality.
rows.threat_or_failure: Researchers or employees cannot report a flaw safely, or sensitive report content leaks through intake and evidence systems.
rows.limitations: Repository case fixtures do not test a live mailbox, portal, encryption key, or responder rota.

rows.capability: Every accepted report is qualified, analyzed, scored consistently, and linked to exact affected products and supported versions.
rows.threat_or_failure: A malformed, duplicate, mis-scoped, or incorrectly scored report drives the wrong priority or product impact decision.
rows.limitations: Synthetic CVSS and impact evidence does not prove analyst expertise or reproduction quality.

rows.capability: A named product owner evaluates remediation, mitigation, transfer, or governed acceptance and tracks the decision to closure.
rows.threat_or_failure: A confirmed vulnerability remains open, is silently ignored, or receives an unowned and permanent risk acceptance.
required_evidence: exact current exception when risk is accepted
rows.limitations: A case deadline does not prove remedy quality, deployment, or customer uptake.

rows.capability: Affected stakeholders receive an accurate advisory or equivalent notice with supported-product scope and remedy guidance.
rows.threat_or_failure: Customers remain exposed because disclosure is missing, inconsistent with affected versions, or lacks actionable remediation guidance.
rows.limitations: The profile does not assess legal sufficiency, notification reach, or customer remediation.

rows.capability: The charter, organizational model, staffing, tooling, procedures, support lifecycle, product registry, and baseline metrics are reviewed together.
rows.threat_or_failure: Basic case handling appears successful while unsupported products, missing dependencies, resource shortages, or procedural drift remain invisible.
rows.limitations: This row checks current evidence, not whether the operating model is optimally staffed.

rows.capability: Internal and downstream stakeholders participate in rehearsed incident communication and coordinated vulnerability decisions.
rows.threat_or_failure: A multi-team or supplier vulnerability causes contradictory decisions, premature disclosure, or missed downstream notification.
rows.limitations: A tabletop exercise cannot prove behavior during every live multi-party incident.

rows.capability: The PSIRT looks for unreported and internally found vulnerabilities and links component intelligence to its product inventory.
rows.threat_or_failure: The program reacts only to external reports and misses vulnerabilities in embedded components or internal findings.
rows.limitations: SBOM and KEV adapters cover selected inputs and do not prove complete discovery coverage.

rows.capability: A maintained reproduction environment and expert escalation path support repeatable analysis of relevant product versions.
rows.threat_or_failure: Analysts cannot reproduce a report safely or consistently and therefore misclassify impact or delay response.
rows.limitations: This repository does not execute exploit content or validate a production reproduction lab.

rows.capability: Formal remedy release, notification, and coordination plans bind exact affected releases to a predictable response workflow.
rows.threat_or_failure: A technically correct fix is released inconsistently, without coordinated notice, or for the wrong supported product line.
rows.limitations: Release-integrity controls do not establish the PSIRT communication process.

rows.capability: The PSIRT measures intake, triage, remediation, disclosure, and channel health and trains its team using reviewed feedback.
rows.threat_or_failure: Repeated delays and communication failures persist because service performance and responder readiness are not measured.
rows.limitations: Repository catalog metrics are not PSIRT operating metrics and must not populate this row automatically.

rows.capability: Long-running policies, funding, staffing, tooling, and cost evidence support both normal vulnerability workload and severe incidents.
rows.threat_or_failure: A program handles routine cases but collapses under concurrent or high-impact product incidents.
rows.limitations: FIRST notes that capability maturity is not the same as capacity; both need independent evidence.

rows.capability: The PSIRT maintains direct finder, peer, supplier, customer, and community engagement and uses stakeholder metrics for improvement.
rows.threat_or_failure: Weak external relationships delay coordinated disclosure, reduce report quality, or hide downstream impact.
rows.limitations: Relationship quality and community trust cannot be inferred from contact volume alone.

rows.capability: Proactive product, component, exploit, conference, publication, and researcher monitoring produces measured and reviewable discovery outcomes.
rows.threat_or_failure: Emerging product vulnerabilities become public or exploited before the organization connects them to affected products.
rows.limitations: No finite intelligence source set proves that all unknown vulnerabilities will be found.

rows.capability: Advanced incident handling coordinates severe or multi-product vulnerabilities, preserves evidence, and validates recovery across affected releases.
rows.threat_or_failure: A widespread vulnerability triggers uncoordinated destructive action, incomplete impact analysis, or premature recovery.
rows.limitations: Offline response-plan validation does not prove distributed containment or business recovery.

rows.capability: Multi-party disclosure playbooks and release metrics demonstrate predictable, accurate, and improving stakeholder outcomes.
rows.threat_or_failure: Complex coordination leaks embargoed information, publishes conflicting guidance, or repeats known release delays.
rows.limitations: Metric improvement does not by itself prove advisory accuracy or stakeholder satisfaction.

rows.capability: Development, validation, legal, support, communications, executive, and other stakeholder groups receive role-specific recurring PSIRT education.
rows.threat_or_failure: Non-PSIRT stakeholders mishandle reports, evidence, remediation, or disclosure because responsibilities are unfamiliar.
rows.limitations: Training completion is not proof of correct behavior during a real vulnerability response.
